A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of TokenTrace with matching methods and main experiments. v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–14; v2 ends after its references and omits that material. This is an observable document omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution experiments, ablations, robustness tests, security measurements and image-fidelity comparisons in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original attribution results, incremental-learning experiments, ablations and distortion tests in Section 4, Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8.

M1.justification: Both retain dual perturbation of text embeddings and initial noise, query-based CLIP decoding, and the same four-loss objective. TokenTraceP remains evaluated with prompt weighting. Omitted pseudocode and variant specifications establish reduced documentation, not an altered method.

E1.justification: WikiArt, ImageNet, the DreamBooth preliminary visualization, and two-customized/four-general-concept tasks remain. v2 omits the clean, zero-watermark negative-image scenario from Section 10 and the five-concept complex-prompt examples in Figures 14–15.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. Removing supplementary Table 5 eliminates the FID comparison against Original LDM, ProMark and CustomMark; Original LDM has no corresponding retained benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: v2 removes the balanced watermarked/clean-image evaluation with TPR, FPR and F1 measurements in Section 10, and the ImageNet FID evaluation in Section 13. These are substantive losses of evaluation protocols. Settings for retained experiments, including training budgets and attribution metrics, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplement's false-positive security analysis, complex-prompt fidelity study and detailed per-concept failure cases disappear. These examined specificity, visual degradation and weakly rendered concepts. The main loss, secret-length, concept-count and distortion ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experiments. The omitted TPR, FPR and F1 values are performance measurements, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main tables and retained plots preserve their results. Omitted results include TPR 92.75%, FPR 0.00% and F1 96.20%, plus Table 5 FIDs: Original LDM 13.28, ProMark 17.63, CustomMark 14.73 and TokenTrace 14.98. Additional per-concept results, including 60% attribution for 'sunny' and 'hills', also disappear.

T1.justification: v1's Equations 12–14 explicitly define separate object/style perturbations and the scaled style embedding for TokenTraceP; these mathematical specifications are omitted. Equations 1–11 remain equivalent, including the merely notational change from L_CE to L_BCE. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about dual-domain watermarking, independent multi-concept attribution, superior attribution performance, visual fidelity and robustness. Removing supporting experiments does not itself revise these claims.

C2.justification: v2 loses the explanation of concept overpowering and prompt weighting, the explicit limitation that retrieval depends on a concept's visual clarity, and the supplementary interpretation of fidelity degradation. Section 3 adds a brief controlled-generation provenance description, but it does not replace these substantive explanations and qualifications.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, TokenTraceP's default scaling factor of 1.1, preliminary-experiment details, dataset examples and extensive training/inference prompt templates are omitted. Main hyperparameters remain, but references to supplementary implementation details persist without the referenced material.

R1.justification: v2 adds MALP to the proactive manipulation-localization discussion. References to Bui et al.'s semantic-collapse work, Heusel et al.'s FID work and van der Maaten and Hinton's t-SNE work disappear with supplementary content. The main positioning against prior attribution methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Omitting supplementary Sections 6–14 substantially contracts the document's explanatory structure, removing algorithm walkthroughs, dataset construction discussion and prompt documentation. Retained main sections are largely unchanged, with localized wording, affiliation, notation and figure-reference corrections.

P2.justification: Figures 10–16, Table 5, three algorithm displays and Listing 1 disappear. Supplementary Figure 9 duplicated the retained Figure 1. Main figures and tables are repositioned; Figures 6 and 8 receive typography and axis-label corrections without changing their data.

improvement.justification: The supplied v2 retains the main claims and benchmark scores while removing substantial evidence about false positives, fidelity tradeoffs and failure conditions. It also removes details needed to reproduce the strongest prompt-weighted variant and experimental prompts, while continuing to reference the absent supplement. Limited wording, notation and layout corrections do not compensate for this substantial loss of evidential completeness and reproducibility.
